analysis_trace: Trial NCT07542821 is a randomized parallel-group trial evaluating ConquerFear (metacognitive psychological training) vs Healthy Lifestyle (nutrition/exercise guidance) vs Education-only control in cancer survivors with fear of cancer recurrence (FCR). Primary endpoint: FCRI score change from baseline to 3 months post-intervention (5 months). Secondary: HADS (anxiety/depression) and VR-12 (quality of life).

Evidence base: Retrieved ConquerFear-HK protocol (BMJ Open 2023, PMID 36669845) showing the same intervention structure in Chinese cancer survivors with FCRI as primary outcome and HADS/EORTC-QoL as secondary. Original ConquerFear trial (Butow et al., Psycho-Oncology 2017) demonstrated efficacy vs attention control with sustained FCRI reduction at 3 and 6 months post-therapy. Network meta-analysis (Sage 2024) ranks ConquerFear-HK highest (SUCRA 99.2%) for FCR reduction.

Evidence matching: ConquerFear-HK protocol matches current trial in population (Chinese/Mandarin-speaking cancer survivors), intervention (6-session metacognitive training), and outcomes (FCRI, HADS, QoL). The current trial adds a healthy lifestyle comparator arm not present in prior studies.

Effect size estimation: Original ConquerFear trial showed FCRI total score reduction of ~10 points (moderate-large effect, d~0.5-0.7) vs control at 3 months. Similar effects expected for ConquerFear group here. Healthy lifestyle interventions show smaller effects on FCR (typically d~0.2-0.3) based on exercise/nutrition RCTs in cancer survivors.

HADS prediction: ConquerFear-HK protocol lists HADS as secondary outcome; metacognitive interventions typically reduce anxiety/depression with small-moderate effects (d~0.3-0.5). Healthy lifestyle may improve HADS through physical health benefits but effect likely smaller (d~0.2-0.3).

VR-12 prediction: Limited direct evidence for VR-12 specifically in this population. Generic QoL measures (EORTC-QLQ-C30) in similar trials show small improvements with psychological interventions (d~0.2-0.4) and modest gains with lifestyle interventions. VR-12 physical/mental component scores expected to follow similar patterns.

Key uncertainties: (1) No published results for this specific trial as of cutoff; (2) Healthy lifestyle arm as active comparator is novel vs prior ConquerFear studies; (3) Stratified randomization based on baseline FCR may affect effect estimates; (4) VR-12 less commonly used than SF-36/EORTC in cancer QoL studies.
Safety: Behavioral interventions have minimal safety concerns. No serious adverse events expected.

Trial success prediction: Primary endpoint (FCRI) likely to favor ConquerFear over education control based on consistent prior evidence. Comparison with healthy lifestyle is uncertain. Secondary endpoints likely to show modest benefits favoring psychological intervention.
